title: Loops
bridge: Java's counting loop is `for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) { ... }`: start, keep-going condition, step. `while (condition) { ... }` repeats until false, and `for (String crop : crops)` goes through every item (the "for-each" loop). `break` and `continue` work as elsewhere.

notes: Nested loops make a times table.
while until the goal is reached.

exercises.title: Times table
exercises.prompt: Read a number and print its times table from 1 to 12, like: 7 x 3 = 21
hints: for (int i = 1; i <= 12; i++) System.out.println(n + " x " + i + " = " + n * i);

exercises.title: Count the vowels
exercises.prompt: Write countVowels(String text): how many a, e, i, o, u (capitals count).
hints: Loop i from 0 to text.length() - 1 and look at text.charAt(i).

exercises.title: Savings goal
exercises.prompt: Write monthsToGoal(int goal, int monthly) with a while loop: months of saving until at least goal. If monthly is 0 or less, return -1.

tests.hint_if_fail: With 0 a month the loop never ends: check monthly <= 0 first.

hints: int saved = 0, months = 0; while (saved < goal) { saved += monthly; months++; }

quiz.q: How many times does for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) run?
Which loop goes through every item of an array most simply?

explain: Explain loops to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
